Subject: SCCs & UK addendum — module selection

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal/compliance team is ready to move forward but needs confirmation on SCC module selection and the form of UK transfers. Specifically:

- Will Redwood sign the new EU SCCs (2021) using Module Two (Controller -> Processor) for our controller->processor relationship?
- For subprocessors you use (some are in the US/Canada), do you expect those to be covered under Module Three (Processor -> Processor) or will you act as a Controller in any flows?
- For data transfers to the UK, do you execute the UK Addendum or would you request us to sign/execute the ICO's IDTA?

We also need the completed Annex I/II/III info and a proposed DPA so our team can validate. Last ask: are you willing to accept limited redlines to the liability clause (cap and carve-outs)?

Can you get us a consolidated packet (DPA + SCC selection + Annexes) this week? Our target close is Oct 10.

Thanks,
Simon
Simon Hart
Head of Legal Ops — Acme Health
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Date: 2025-10-01T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: SCCs & UK addendum — module selection

Hi Simon,

Thanks — noted. Short answers up front:

- Redwood acts as a processor for customer-controlled data. For EU transfers we will use the EU SCCs with Module Two (Controller -> Processor) for the primary agreement with Acme.
- Where Redwood engages subprocessors that themselves receive Customer Data and act as processors, we will flow down Module Three (Processor -> Processor) to those subprocessors as appropriate. We do not treat those subprocessors as controllers for customer-controlled data.
- For UK transfers we can execute the EU SCCs plus the standard UK Addendum (we also support IDTA on a case-by-case basis, but the UK Addendum is our default).

I've attached our current DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf) and a short SCC execution form that shows the module mapping and processor/subprocessor list. Please review the Annex I/II/III fields in the DPA — we can fill in the processing details and a data flow diagram once you confirm the scope (products/environments and any special categories).

About liability/redlines: we generally keep a standard cap but are open to narrow, reciprocal language for negotiated enterprise deals. If you can flag the specific clauses you want to edit, we'll have legal review and come back with track changes.

Attached: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf; Redwood_SCC_Execution_Form.pdf

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Irene,

Appreciate the quick reply. A couple of clarifying items from our compliance reviewers:

- Subprocessors: can you confirm the current list and which countries they operate from? We saw references to a logging/analytics vendor (US) and a hosting partner (Netherlands/US).
- Transfers: our privacy team wants explicit confirmation that the UK Addendum + SCCs will be treated as sufficient without additional contractual measures. If RDW believes supplementary technical/organizational measures are required, please list them.
- Annexes: we will need Annex II to include lawful basis, processing purposes, categories of data subjects and categories of personal data.
- Liability: specifically, our counsel will ask about a mutual carve-out for security incidents caused by gross negligence or willful misconduct. Are you able to accept that carve-out?

If you can provide an annotated DPA (track changes) and a proposed execution plan (DocuSign link or timeline) by Oct 7, we can route for internal sign-off.

Thanks,
Simon
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Hart <simon.hart@acme-health.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-03T16:20:00Z
Subject: RE: SCCs & UK addendum — module selection and Annex II details

Hi Simon / Irene,

Looping in since this is a legal question. Wanted to be explicit and practical so your compliance team can see our position:

1) Module selection
- Primary controller -> processor relationship: EU SCCs Module Two (Controller -> Processor). We will complete the relevant modules and execution form.
- Processor -> processor flows to subprocessors: we will flow down Module Three to any subprocessor that further processes Customer Data.

2) UK transfers
- Redwood will execute the EU SCCs with the standard UK Addendum (our template) for transfers to/from the UK. If you prefer the ICO IDTA we can evaluate but the UK Addendum is our default and accepted by many customers.

3) Supplementary measures
- Legally, for most routable transfers the SCCs + contractual commitments + our technical controls (encryption at rest/in transit, strict key management, access controls, SOC 2 controls) have been accepted as sufficient. If your team requires documented supplementary measures, we will provide a short memo listing: encryption key separation, regional isolation options, and audit logging with retention controls.

4) Subprocessors and countries
- Current subprocessors: HostingPartner Ltd (Netherlands, US regions), Loglytics Inc (US), MetricsCo (US & EU). We will provide a filtered, exportable list and will add clause in the DPA with 30-day notice of any additions.

5) Liability carve-out
- We cannot accept a unilateral broad carve-out that removes remedies for security incidents caused by gross negligence. However, we are open to a mutual, limited carve-out for indirect damages and are willing to accept a negotiated cap tied to a short multiple of fees subject to specific carve-outs for willful misconduct, gross negligence, and breaches of confidentiality. If your counsel can propose language, we'll expedite review.

6) Timeline & execution
- I'll prepare annotated DPA with the module selection marked and return a DocuSign-ready packet by EOD Oct 6. Execution target: Oct 10 as requested.

Attachments to follow: Redwood_SCC_Execution_Form.pdf; Annex_2_Data_Transfers.docx

Regards,
